title: DFJ12 8-round AES-128 / aes128-8r-single-chosen-key-streamed-dfj2012

target.description: 8 nonlinear AES-128 rounds; Figures 4/9 include the final public linear output map and the subspace condition is transported through it. Figure 1/source Section 2 use AK before SB. This pair-finding endpoint is not unknown-master-key recovery.

setting.key_relation: One freely chosen AES-128 master key used for BOTH messages. No key difference or related-key oracle; the key schedule is standard.
setting.plaintext_model: Construct (m,m-prime,k) such that m XOR m-prime lies in the prescribed four-byte-dimensional input subspace and the ciphertext difference lies in the prescribed four-byte-dimensional output subspace.
assumptions: The adversary chooses one key; not a fixed known-key game and not a secret-key recovery game.

Reduced-round source uses AK before SB and a public linear terminal map. The finite AppendixA witness matches with terminalMC and finalARK; the AppendixB absolute End row has a separate local discrepancy, while its output difference matches.
setting.reference_model: Single-chosen-key limited-birthday restricted-pair construction versus an ideal keyed permutation; source generic comparator 2^64 basic operations.

success.description: No numerical overall success is stated for this eight-round streamed AES128 endpoint. The source builds2^24 middle candidates and expects one to pass the2^-24 outbound model; no Poisson hit rate is inferred. Preserve its own resource vector and the existing AppendixB absolute terminal-state witness conflict. The seven-round greater-than99.96% list claim is not borrowed for this different construction. Streaming changes storage, not the success event.

field_conflicts.description: Independent FIPS-checked finite AES evaluation agrees with all16 preterminal state values and the displayed output XOR, but neither the present/absent terminalMixColumns nor present/absent finalAddRoundKey combinations reproduce both printed absolute End values for the given masterkey. Retain the source End row without silently replacing it; this does not establish a wrong attack complexity.
